question: Will the U.S. naval blockade halting Iran's seaborne crude oil exports still be in effect on October 15, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is YES: the blockade has been enforced continuously since July 14 (Wikipedia timeline; Bessent's 'ironclad' remark in early October), and only 10.7 days of the window remain. The June precedent shows things can move fast: Trump announced the deal on June 14 and CENTCOM lifted the blockade on June 18. But Iran's October 4 reply through Qatar was hardline. It insists the US act first (sanctions relief, frozen funds, an end to the shipping blockade) and rules out nuclear talks. Trump is talking about military options, which points to escalation rather than a lift. Polymarket's 'US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15' contract trades at about 12¢ (about $0.85M volume on that bucket; $35.6M on the event). That contract resolves on a US announcement, not an operational lift, so it is close to our NO condition and slightly broader. My estimate is roughly in line with it.
calls.dossier:
- Blockade history (Wikipedia, '2026 United States naval blockade of Iran'): first imposed Apr 13, 2026 after the Islamabad talks failed. Trump announced a deal Jun 14; CENTCOM removed the blockade Jun 18 (4 days from announcement to operational lift). Trump announced reinstatement Jul 13; enforced from Jul 14-15. WSJ (Sep 7) says it halted new Iranian Gulf exports. More than 100 vessels redirected by late September.
- Early Oct 2026 (Iran International, ~Oct 4): Treasury Sec. Bessent calls the blockade 'ironclad' and says Iran has 'no oil shipments at sea this week'. 'Operation Economic Outcast' sanctions are expanding to the automotive and rail sectors. Trump says 'all options' are on the table and renewed military operations are 'possible', maybe before the November midterms. The Theodore Roosevelt CSG and Makin Island ARG are heading to the region.
- Sep 23-26 (The National, Gulf News): Iran submitted via Qatar a 7-day roadmap: a 60-day regionwide ceasefire, phased Hormuz reopening, and an end to the US blockade.
- ~Sep 25 (Reuters via Business Standard/Arab News): US and Iran discussing a phased deal in New York, Qatar mediating. Neither side wants to give up its leverage first. The New York talks ended without agreement.
- Oct 4 (Xinhua/report.az, Iranian MFA spokesman Baghaei): Iran sent its reply to the US proposal (roadmap/timetable based on the Islamabad framework) through Qatar. It effectively rules out resuming nuclear talks and demands concrete US steps first: a complete end to obstacles on Iranian shipping, removal of sanctions, an end to military interventions.
- Mechanism for NO: a deal announcement can produce an operational lift within days (June precedent).
- Status-quo outcome: blockade still enforced (YES). Under the fine print, YES also holds if no credible source reports a lift.
- Base-rate notes: in about 5.7 months since Apr 13, the blockade was lifted once (June) and reimposed once. Over 10-day windows during active blockade periods, about 1 of ~15 windows contained a lift. That is computed over all windows; windows following a reported deal announcement are a different, much higher class.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off wire services (Reuters/Bloomberg/AP) or tanker trackers reporting the formal or operational status. Individual escorted transits do not count as a lift.
- Human market: a Polymarket event 'US announces end of Iranian blockade by...?' exists (opened Sep 24; resolves on a US announcement, not an operational lift; dated buckets Oct 15/Oct 31/Nov 30/Dec 31/Mar 31). The bucket price is withheld here to avoid anchoring.
- Event window: now -> 23:59 UTC Oct 15, 2026 per the criteria. As of Oct 5 06:11 UTC, the blockade has already run ~83 days since Jul 14, and ~10.7 days remain in the window.
- Searched, not found: any report of a scheduled new round of direct or indirect talks in the Oct 5-15 window, and any US statement on a conditional lift timetable.
calls.reference_class: Short-horizon (~10-day) persistence of an active wartime naval blockade under ongoing stalled indirect talks; blockade lift events in 2026 = 1 (June) across ~5.5 months of blockade

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on every fact: the blockade has been active since Jul 14, Iran's Oct 4 reply was hardline, Trump rejected Iran's conditions and points to post-midterm resolution, there is the June precedent of a fast lift, and Polymarket's Oct 15 bucket is ~12% on an announcement-based contract. The only difference is judgment, 0.89 vs 0.90: how much the market's broader announcement-based NO condition justifies sitting above its implied 88%. With no web access I could not re-check the market price. I take the reading that an announcement would likely become a formal suspension, so the contract is close to ours but slightly broader, and the hardline Oct 4 exchange makes a deal within 10 days unlikely. That gives 0.90.
